subject: error when variable declared in model block but not in parameters block

messages.author: 206c95168ffdfa45
messages.subject: error when variable declared in model block but not in parameters block
parts:
I'm a stan beginner trying to fit a hierarchical logistic regression (with random intercepts) using RStan. I was able to get the model to work when I put the vector of random intercepts into the parameters block. This results in a large output. I would prefer to exclude the intercepts from the output, which I understand can be done by declaring the variable inside the model block instead of in the parameters block. Yet, when I do that the sampler fails due to the following error:
[594] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[595] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                          
[596] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[597] "Exception thrown at line 22: stan::math::normal_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!"                                     
[598] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[599] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified." 

Why does it fail in the one case but not the other?

Here is the code that works:
data {
    int<lower=0> N; #number of total observations
    int<lower=1> D; #dimensionality of covariates, excluding intercept
    int<lower=1> K; #number of clusters
    matrix[N,D] X; #covariate design matrix
    int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N]; #binary outcome
    int<lower=1,upper=K> id[N]; #cluster id
}
parameters {
    real alpha; #intercept
    vector[D] beta; #fixed effects
    real<lower=0> sigma; #stdev of random intercepts
    vector[K] rand_ints;
}
model {
  vector[N] eta;
  for(d in 1:D) beta[d]~cauchy(0,5);
  # prior for random effect stdev
  sigma~cauchy(0,5);
  #prior for random effects
  for(k in 1:K){
    rand_ints[k]~normal(0,sigma);
  }
  for(n in 1:N){
    eta[n]<-alpha + X[n]*beta + rand_ints[id[n]];
  }
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(eta);
}


Here is the code that throws the error (only change is where declaration of rand_ints):

    int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N]; #binary outcome

}

    real alpha; #intercept

}

  vector[K] rand_ints;
  vector[N] eta;
  for(d in 1:D) beta[d]~cauchy(0,5);
  # prior for random effect stdev
  sigma~cauchy(0,5);
  #prior for random effects

    rand_ints[k]~normal(0,sigma);
  }
  for(n in 1:N){
    eta[n]<-alpha + X[n]*beta + rand_ints[id[n]];
  }
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(eta);
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: error when variable declared in model block but not in parameters block
parts:
On Sunday, May 8, 2016 at 2:55:23 AM UTC-4, Will Townes wrote:
I'm a stan beginner trying to fit a hierarchical logistic regression (with random intercepts) using RStan. I was able to get the model to work when I put the vector of random intercepts into the parameters block. This results in a large output. I would prefer to exclude the intercepts from the output, which I understand can be done by declaring the variable inside the model block instead of in the parameters block. Yet, when I do that the sampler fails due to the following error:

That is a misunderstanding. You can exclude an intermediate quantity from the output by putting it in the model block or a local block within the transformed parameters block. But in this case the intercepts are primitive in which case they must be declared in the model block. The only way to exclude them from the output is by specifying

stan(filename, pars = "rand_ints", include = FALSE)
[597] "Exception thrown at line 22: stan::math::normal_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!"

This tells you that in line 22, the left hand side of the ~ is NaN, which is guaranteed by the structure of the second model because rand_ints is not defined before it is referenced.

Ben
